questions.question: Ramu used to spend 72% of his income. His income has increased by 12%, and he increases his expenditure by 5%. If Ramu earlier saved y and after the increases he now saves x, then what is the value of \(\rm \left(\frac{x-y}{y}\times 100\right)\) %?
questions.questionHtml: Ramu used to spend 72% of his income. His income has increased by 12%, and he increases his expenditure by 5%. If Ramu earlier saved y  and after the increases he now saves x, then what is the value of\(\rm \left(\frac{x-y}{y}\times 100\right)\)%?
questions.solution:
Initial income = 100,

Initial expenditure = 72; Initial savings (y) = 100-72 = 28

New income = 100 × 1.12 = 112, New expenditure = 72 × 1.05 = 75.6,

New savings (x) = 112 - 75.6 = 36.4, 

Percentage change in savings = (8.4 / 28) × 100 = 30%

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 65% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 3% of the votes were decided to be invalid. A candidate got 81965 votes which are 65% of the total valid votes. What is the total number of votes enrolled in that election?
questions.questionHtml: In an election between two candidates, 65% of the voters cast their votes, out of which 3% of the votes were decided to be invalid. A candidate got 81965 votes which are 65% of the total valid votes. What is the total number of votes enrolled in that election?
questions.solution:
Given:

65% of the voters cast their votes

3% of the votes were decided to be invalid

A candidate got 81965 votes which are 65% of the total valid votes

Concept Used:

The concept of percentage  is a number or ratio that can be expressed as a fraction of 100

Calculations:

Let the total number of votes enrolled be x

65% of the voters cast their votes

⇒ Number of votes cast = \(\frac{x\times65}{100}\)

3% of the votes were decided to be invalid

⇒ That means 97% of votes cast are valid 

⇒ Number of valid votes = Number of Votes cast x 97% = \(\frac{x\times65}{100}\times\frac{97}{100}=\frac{x\times65\times 97}{10000}\)

A candidate got 81965 votes which are 65% of the total valid votes

⇒ A candidate gets votes = 65% of total valid votes = \(\frac{x\times65\times 97}{10000}\times \frac{65}{100}=\frac{x\times65\times 97\times 65}{1000000}\)

According to the question,

⇒ A candidate got 81965 votes

so,

⇒ \(\frac{x\times65\times 97\times 65}{1000000} = 81965\)

⇒ \(\frac{x}{1000000}= 0.2\)

⇒ x = 200000

⇒ Hence, The number of votes total enrolled is 200000.

Shortcut TrickCalculation:

The candidate's votes represent 65% of the valid votes

⇒ valid votes = 81965 / 0.65 = 126100

Valid votes represent 97% of total votes cast (100 - 3)%

⇒ Total votes cast = 126100 / 0.97 = 130000

Total votes cast represent 65% of total votes enrolled

⇒ total votes enrolled = 130000 / 0.65 = 200,000

∴ The total number of votes enrolled in that election is 200,000.

questions.question: A man spends 15% of his income on house rent, 60% of the rest on household expenses and saves the rest. If he saves ₹52,500, what is his total income (in ₹, rounded off to the nearest tens)?
questions.questionHtml: A man spends 15% of his income on house rent, 60% of the rest on household expenses and saves the rest. If he saves ₹52,500, what is his total income (in ₹, rounded off to the nearest tens)?
questions.solution:
Given:

A man spends 15% of his income on house rent, 60% of the rest on household expenses and saves the rest.

Formula used:

Savings = total income - Total expenses 

Calculation:

Let the person's total income be x.

Then, the amount he spends on house rent is 0.15x

The amount he spends on households expenses is 0.6 × 0.15x

Therefore, the amount he save is (x - 0.15x - 0.6 × 0.15x) = 52500.

Solving for x,

0.34x = 52500

\(x=\frac{52500}{0.34}=154411.74\)

∴ The total income rounded off to the nearest tens is Rs. 1,54,410

questions.question: If A is 28% less than B and C is 25% less than the sum of A and B, then by what percentage will C be more than A (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.questionHtml: If A is 28% less than B and C is 25% less than the sum of A and B, then by what percentage will C be more than A (correct to one decimal place)?

A is 28% less than B

C is 25% less than the sum of A and B

⇒ 25A = 18B

⇒ A/B = 18/25

⇒ A : B = 18 : 25

Let A and B is 18x and 25x

4C = 3 × 43x

⇒ C = 32.25x

C – A = 32.25x – 18x

⇒ 14.25x

(14.25x/18x) × 100

⇒ 79.166 ≈ 79.2%

questions.question: If a reduction of 10% in the price of rice enables a person to obtain 22 kg more for Rs.250, then the original price of rice per kg is ________.
questions.questionHtml: If a reduction of 10% in the price of rice enables a person to obtain 22 kg more for Rs.250, then the original price of rice per kg is ________.
questions.solution:
Given:

A reduction of 10% in the price of rice enables a person to obtain 22 kg more for Rs.250

Concept Used:

A percentage is a number or ratio that can be expressed as a fraction of 100

Calculations:

Let the original price of rice be 100x

⇒ New price= Original Price - 10% of original Price= 100x - 10x= 90x

According to the question,

⇒ \(\frac{250}{90x}-\frac{250}{100x}=22\)

⇒ \(\frac{250\times10-250\times9}{900x}=22\)

⇒ \(\frac{2500-2250}{900x}=22\)

⇒ \(900x=\frac{250}{22}\)

⇒ 100x=\(\frac{250}{22\times9}\)=1.26

Hence, The original price of rice per kg is Rs. 1.26

questions.question: If a number is first increased by 15%, then reduced by 15%, it results in 782. If the same number is first reduced by 25%, then increased by 25% and again reduced by 20%, then what will be the resulting number?
questions.questionHtml: If a number is first increased by 15%, then reduced by 15%, it results in 782. If the same number is first reduced by 25%, then increased by 25% and again reduced by 20%, then what will be the resulting number?
questions.solution:
Given:

A number is first increased by 15%, then reduced by 15%.

Number became 782.

The same number is first reduced by 25%, then increased by 25%, and again reduced by 20%.

Calculation:

Let the number of N.

Number after increased by 15% = N × 115/100 = 23N/20

Number after decreased by 15% = (23N/20) × (85/100) = 1955N / 2000

= 391N/400

Then,

⇒ 391N/400 = 782

⇒ N = 800

New number after reduced by 25% = 800 × 75/100 = 600

New number after increased by 25% = 600 × 125/100 = 750

New number after reduced by 20% = 750 × 80/100 = 600

∴ New number formed is 600.

Alternate MethodLet the original number be y

⇒ y × 115/100 × 85/100 = 782

⇒ y × 23/20 × 17/20 = 782

⇒ y = 800

New number that is first reduced by 25%, then increased by 25%, and again reduced by 20%,

⇒ 800 × 3/4 × 5/4 × 4/5 = 600

∴ The new number formed is 600.

questions.question: When the price of rice increases by 25%, a person increases his expenditure on rice only by 15%. By what percentage should he reduce his consumption of rice so as to be able to maintain the same level of expenditure?
questions.questionHtml: When the price of rice increases by 25%, a person increases his expenditure on rice only by 15%. By what percentage should he reduce his consumption of rice so as to be able to maintain the same level of expenditure?
questions.solution:
Given data:

Increase in rice price = 25%

Increase in expenditure = 15%

Calculation:

We know that Expenditure = Price × Consumption

Alternatively, Consumption = Expenditure ÷ Price

⇒ Consumption = \(115\over 125\) = 0.92

Decrease in consumption = 1 - 0.92 = 0.08 or 8%

∴ The Person has to decrease his consumption by 8% to maintain his level of expenditure.

questions.question: Alloy A contains metals x and y in the ratio 5 ∶ 2 and alloy B contains these metals in the ratio 3 ∶ 4. Alloy C is prepared by mixing A and B in the ratio 4 ∶ 5. The percentage of y in alloy C is:
questions.questionHtml: Alloy A contains metals x and y in the ratio 5 ∶ 2 and alloy B contains these metals in the ratio 3 ∶ 4. Alloy C is prepared by mixing A and B in the ratio 4 ∶ 5. The percentage of y in alloy C is:
questions.solution:
Given:

The ratio of x and y in alloy A = 5 : 2

The ratio of x and y in alloy B = 3 : 4

The ratio of A and B in the alloy C = 4 : 5

Calculation:

Let the quantity of y in alloy C be x.

⇒ Quantity of metal x in alloy A = 5/7

⇒ Quantity of metal y in alloy A = 2/7

⇒ Quantity of metal x in alloy B = 3/7

⇒ Quantity of metal y in alloy B = 4/7

According to the question

The ratio of x and y in alloy C = (5/7 × 4 + 3/7 × 5)/(2/7 × 4 + 4/7 × 5)

⇒ (20/7 + 15/7)/(8/7 + 20/7)

⇒ (35/7)/(28/7)

⇒ 5/4

The ratio of x and y in alloy C = 5 : 4

⇒ Quantity of y in alloy C = 4/9

Percentage of y in alloy C = (4/9 × 100)

⇒ (400/9)

⇒ \(44\frac{4}{9}%\)%

∴ The percentage of y in alloy C is \(44\frac{4}{9}%\)%

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters did not cast their votes and 5% of the votes polled were found invalid. The successful candidate got 52.5% of the valid votes and won by a majority of 1710 votes. The number of voters enrolled on the voters list was:
questions.questionHtml: In an election between two candidates, 10% of the voters did not cast their votes and 5% of the votes polled were found invalid. The successful candidate got 52.5% of the valid votes and won by a majority of 1710 votes. The number of voters enrolled on the voters list was:
questions.solution:
Let total voters be x,

Voters voted = 0.90x,

Valid votes = 0.855x,

Successful candidate votes = 0.525 × 0.855x = 0.448875x,

Other candidate votes = 0.855x - 0.448875x = 0.406125x,

Majority = 1710,

0.448875x - 0.406125x = 1710,

0.04275x = 1710,

x = 1710/0.04275,

x = 40000,

Number of voters enrolled = 40000.

The winning candidate received 60% of the total valid votes in his favour and won the election by 17271 votes. Find the number of registered voters.
questions.solution:
5% of total did not cast votes ⇒ 100 × 95/100 = 95 casted votes

10% of 95 pressed NOTA, 90% of 95 casted votes ⇒ 90/100 × 95 = 9/2 × 19

Difference between them is 60% - 40% = 20%

⇒ 20% of 9/2 × 19 = 17,271 ⇒ 1/5 × 9/2 × 19 = 17,271 ⇒ 1 = 1010

Total voters = 100 = 100 × 1010 = 1,01,000

questions.question: The income of A is 20% less than the income of B and the income of C is 70% of the sum of incomes of A and B. The income of D is 25% more than the income of C. If the difference between the incomes of B and D is Rs. 23000, then what is the income (in Rs.) of A?
questions.questionHtml: The income of A is 20% less than the income of B and the income of C is 70% of the sum of incomes of A and B. The income of D is 25% more than the income of C. If the difference between the incomes of B and D is Rs. 23000, then what is the income (in Rs.) of A?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Income of B = 100 units, then A = 80 units (20% less).

Income of C = 70% of (100 + 80) = 126 units.

Income of D = 125% of 126 = 157.5 units.

Difference (D − B) = 57.5 units → ₹23000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹400.

Income of A = 80 × 400 = ₹32000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹32000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Income of A = Income of B − 20% of Income of B

Income of C = 70% of (Income of A + Income of B)

Income of D = Income of C + 25% of Income of C

Difference between incomes of B and D = ₹23000

Calculations:

⇒ Let the income of B = 100x

⇒ Income of A = 100x − 20x = 80x

⇒ Income of C = 70% of (80x + 100x) = 126x

⇒ Income of D = 126x + 25% of 126x = 157.5x

⇒ Difference between D and B = 157.5x − 100x = 57.5x

⇒ 57.5x = 23000

⇒ x = 23000 ÷ 57.5

⇒ x = 400

⇒ Income of A = 80x = 80 × 400 = 32000

∴ The correct answer is ₹32000.

Additional Information

Base Value in Percentage

When comparing two quantities, the quantity following words like 'than' or 'of' is generally taken as the base (100%).

Successive Percentage Change

If a value is changed by A% and then by B%, the net percentage change is given by A + B + (A × B) ÷ 100.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

It is helpful to remember standard fraction equivalents, such as 20% = 1/5 and 25% = 1/4, for faster calculations.

questions.question: Ramagya spends 22% of his salary on house rent and 75% of the rest on household expenses. If he saves ₹3,705, find his total income (in rupees).
questions.questionHtml: Ramagya spends 22% of his salary on house rent and 75% of the rest on household expenses. If he saves ₹3,705, find his total income (in rupees).
questions.solution:
Given:

Ramagya spends 22% of his salary on house rent.

He spends 75% of the rest on household expenses.

He saves ₹3,705.

Formula Used:

Total income = Savings / (1 - (Percentage spent on house rent + Percentage spent on household expenses of the rest))

Calculation:

Let the total income be ₹X.

Amount spent on house rent = 22% of X = 0.22X

Remaining income after house rent = X - 0.22X = 0.78X

Amount spent on household expenses = 75% of remaining income = 0.75 × 0.78X = 0.585X

Total savings = Remaining income - Amount spent on household expenses

⇒ 0.78X - 0.585X = ₹3,705

⇒ 0.195X = ₹3,705

⇒ X = ₹3,705 / 0.195

⇒ X = ₹19,000

Ramagya's total income is ₹19,000.

questions.question: A family earns Rs. 75,000, out of which 10% is saved. 30% of the remaining expenditure is incurred on education, while Rs. 30,375 is spent on health and the remaining amount is spent on food. What is the percentage of food expenditure to the total income?
questions.questionHtml: A family earns Rs. 75,000, out of which 10% is saved. 30% of the remaining expenditure is incurred on education, while Rs. 30,375 is spent on health and the remaining amount is spent on food. What is the percentage of food expenditure to the total income?
questions.solution:
A family  total savings = 75000 × (10/100) = Rs.7500

Remaining amount = 75000 - 7500 = Rs.67500

Spent on education = 67500 × (30/100) = Rs.20250

Remaining amount after spent on education & health = 67500 - 20250 - 30375 = Rs.16875

Amount spent on Food = Rs.16875

Required percentage = (16875/75000) × 100 = 22.5%

questions.question: A marketing agent earns a commission of 2% on first Rs. 2,00,000 1.5% on next Rs. 2,00,000 and 1% on the remaining amount of sales made in a month. If the sales achieved by agent for the month of April 2018 are Rs. 5, 68,000 the commission earned is:
questions.questionHtml: A marketing agent earns a commission of 2% on first Rs. 2,00,000 1.5% on next Rs. 2,00,000 and 1% on the remaining amount of sales made in a month. If the sales achieved by agent for the month of April 2018 are Rs. 5, 68,000 the commission earned is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A marketing agent earns a commission of 2% on first Rs. 2,00,000 1.5% on next

Rs. 2,00,000 and 1% on the remaining amount of sales made in a month

Calculation:

Commission rate on first Rs. 2,00,000 is 2%

Commission rate of next Rs. 2,00,000 is 1.5%

Commission rate on above 4,00,000 is 1%

According to the question

Commission earned by agent

= 2,00,000 × (2/100) + 2,00,000 × (1.5/100) + (5,68,000 – 4,00,000) × (1/100)

= 4000 + 3000 + 1,68,000 × (1/100)

= 7000 + 1680

= 8680

Thus the correct answer is Rs.8680.

questions.question: A number is decreased by 20% to get another number. The number so obtained is increased by 200% to get a third number. The difference of the third number and the original number is what percentage more or less than the difference of second and the third number?
questions.questionHtml: A number is decreased by 20% to get another number. The number so obtained is increased by 200% to get a third number. The difference of the third number and the original number is what percentage more or less than the difference of second and the third number?
questions.solution:
Let the 1st number be Q,  2nd number = Q(1 - 20%) = 0.8Q,  3rd number = 0.8Q(1 + 200%) = 2.4Q

The difference between the  3rd number and the original number = 2.4Q - Q = 1.4Q

The difference between the 2nd and 3rd number = 2.4Q - 0.8Q = 1.6Q

Now, % less = \(\frac {1.6Q - 1.4Q}{1.6Q} \times 100\%\) = 12.5%

questions.question: The income of X is 42% more than that of Y and the income of Z is 45% less than the sum of the incomes of X and Y. By what per cent is the income of Z less than the income of X (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.questionHtml: The income of X is 42% more than that of Y and the income of Z is 45% less than the sum of the incomes of X and Y. By what per cent is the income of Z less than the income of X (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Given:

The income of X is 42% more than that of Y

The income of Z is 45% less than the sum of the income of X and Y

Formula used:

\({GM\%\ =\ {GM\over TM}}\ \times 100\)     Where, GM = Gain marks, and TM = Total marks

Calculation:

Let the income of X, Y, and Z, be X, Y, and Z respectively

According to the question

⇒ X = \({142Y\over 100}\)

⇒ 100X = 142Y     ----(1)

⇒ Z = \({55\ \times (X\ +\ Y)\over 100}\)

⇒ 100Z = 55X + 55Y     ----(2)

By equation (1) and (2)

⇒ 100Z = 55X + \({55\ \times 100X\over 142}\)

⇒ 14200Z = 7810X + 5500X

⇒ 14200Z = 13310X

⇒ \({X\over Z}\ =\ {14200\over 13310}\)

The required percentage = \({14200x\ -\ 13310x\over 14200}\ \times 100\ =\ 6.26\%\ \approx 6.3\%\)

∴ The required result will be 6.3%.

questions.question: A reduction of 20% in the rate of sugar enables Sudhir to get 6 kg more sugar for Rs. 960. What is the reduced rate of sugar per kg?
questions.questionHtml: A reduction of 20% in the rate of sugar enables Sudhir to get 6 kg more sugar for Rs. 960. What is the reduced rate of sugar per kg?
questions.solution:
Given:

20% reduction results to 6 kg more sugar.

Concept used:

Application of percentage

Calculation:

Let the previous price of the sugar be Rs. P for the certain amount R kg.

Now, previously (R + 6) kg could have been acquired at = 960 ÷ 0.8 = Rs. 1200

So, Rs. (1200 - 960) = Rs. 240 results to 6 kg.

Hence, previous price of sugar = 240 ÷ 6 = Rs. 40 per kg

So, at Rs. 960, One could get = 960 ÷ 40 = 24kg sugar

Now, recent price of sugar = 960 ÷ (24 + 6) = Rs. 32

∴ The reduced rate of sugar is Rs. 32 per kg.

Shortcut Trick 

  Fraction OLD NEW
Price 20% = -(1/5) 5 4
Quantity 25% = +(1/4) 4 5
Expenditure ( E = P × Q ) Remains Unchanged 20 20

Quantity is increased in such way that the expenditure remains same.

∴ If, Old Quantity = 4x, then New Quantity = 5x

So,

Increase in Quantity = 5x - 6x = x

According to Question,

⇒ x = 6kg.

⇒ Old Quantity = 4x = 4 × 6 = 24kg

⇒ New Quantity = 5x = 5 × 6 = 30kg

∴ New rate per kg = Rs. 960/30kg = Rs. 32/kg

questions.question: The total consumption of sugar was 20 kg per month for a family. As the price of sugar increased by 35%, the family reduced its consumption so that the expenditure on sugar is increased only by 8%. By how much was the consumption of sugar per month reduced due to increase in the price of sugar?
questions.questionHtml: The total consumption of sugar was 20 kg per month for a family. As the price of sugar increased by 35%, the family reduced its consumption so that the expenditure on sugar is increased only by 8%. By how much was the consumption of sugar per month reduced due to increase in the price of sugar?
questions.solution:
Given:

The total consumption of sugar was 20 kg per month for a family.

the price of sugar increased by 35% and the expenditure on sugar is increased only by 8%

Concept:

Consumption × Price = Expenditure

Increment/Decrement in percentage = {(100 ± increase/decrease)/100} × Value

Solution:

Let the Price of sugar be Rs. 100 per kg

So, Initial expenditure is

⇒ 20 × 100 = Rs. 2000

The increased price of the sugar per kg is

⇒ (135/100) × 100 = Rs. 135

The increased Expenditure is

⇒ (108/100) × 2000

⇒ 2160

Now,

⇒ Consumption = Expenditure/Price

⇒ Consumption = 2160/135

⇒ Consumption = 16

Reduction in consumption is 20 - 16 = 4 kg

∴ the consumption of sugar per month reduced is 4 kg.

The winning candidate got 56% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 1,458 votes. What is the total number of voters enrolled in the voter list?

The winning candidate got 56% of the valid votes and won the election by a margin of 1,458 votes. What is the total number of voters enrolled in the voter list?
questions.solution:
Let, the total enrolled voters be x

valid vote = (90/100) × (9x/10) ⇒ 81x/100

The winning candidate got 56% of the polled vote means the looser got (100 – 56) = 44% vote

{(56/100) × (81x/100)} - {(44/100) × (81x/100)} = 1458 ⇒ (81x/100) × {(56 – 44)/100} = 1458 ⇒ (81 × 12)x/10000 = 1458 ⇒ x = (1458× 10000)/(81 × 12) ⇒ x = 15000

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 85% of the voters cast their votes, out which 4% of the votes were declared invalid. A candidate got 6936 votes which were 85% of the valid votes. Find the total number of voters enrolled in that election.
questions.questionHtml: In an election between two candidates, 85% of the voters cast their votes, out which 4% of the votes were declared invalid. A candidate got 6936 votes which were 85% of the valid votes. Find the total number of voters enrolled in that election.
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

85% of the voters cast their votes in an election

4% of the votes were declared invalid 

A candidate got 6936 votes which were 85% of the valid votes

CALCULATION:

Let us assume the  total number of voters enrolled be 100x

Number of voters cast their votes = 85% of 100x 

⇒ 85/100 × 100x = 85x 

Number of invalid votes = 4% of  85x

⇒ 4/100 × 85x = 3.4x 

Number of valid votes = 85x - 3.4x = 81.6x

Now, according to the given question we have

A  candidate got no. of votes = 6936 which were 85% of the valid votes

⇒ 85% of the valid votes = 0.85 × 81.6x = 69.36x

⇒ 69.36x = 6936 

⇒ x = 6936/69.36 = 100 

Now, the total number of voters enrolled = 100x 

⇒ 100 × 100 = 10,000

Hence, the total number of voters enrolled in that election is 10,000.

questions.question: The income of A is 40% less than that of B, and the income of C is 40% more than 30% of the combined income of A and B. By what percentage is C's income more than the income of A?
questions.questionHtml: The income of A is 40% less than that of B, and the income of C is 40% more than 30% of the combined income of A and B. By what percentage is C's income more than the income of A?
questions.solution:
Given:

The income of A is 40% less than that of B

income of C is 40% more than 30% of the combined income of A and B

Calculation:

40% = 2/5  

By this, A = 3 and B = 5

A and B combine = 8

30 % of A and B combine = 8 x 3/10 = 12/5

C = 12/5 x 140/100 = 84/25 

% of C's income more than the income of A = [(84/25 - 3)/3] x 100 = 12 %

therefore, % of C's income more than the income of A is 12%

questions.question: A father gives 8% of his monthly income to both his sons as pocket money. The elder son gets 85% of the total amount given to both sons. He spends 90% of the amount and saves Rs. 17. What is the monthly income of his father?
questions.questionHtml: A father gives 8% of his monthly income to both his sons as pocket money. The elder son gets 85% of the total amount given to both sons. He spends 90% of the amount and saves Rs. 17. What is the monthly income of his father?
questions.solution:

questions.question: A's salary is 15% less than B's salary. B's salary is 30% less than C's salary. By how much percent approximately, is C's salary more than A's salary?
questions.questionHtml: A's salary is 15% less than B's salary. B's salary is 30% less than C's salary. By how much percent approximately, is C's salary more than A's salary?
questions.solution:
Given:

A's salary is 15% less than B's salary. B's salary is 30% less than C's salary.

Calculation:

A's salary is 15% less than B's salary ⇒ A's salary : B's salary = 85 : 100 = 17 : 20

B's salary is 30% less than C's salary ⇒ B's salary : C's salary = 70 : 100 = 7 : 10

∴ Salary of A : B : C = 17 × 7 : 20 × 7 : 20 × 10 = 119 : 140 : 200

⇒  A's salary : C's salary = 119 : 200

∴ C's salary is more than A's salary by (200 - 119)/119 × 100

⇒ (81/119) × 100

⇒ 68%

questions.question: Instead of increasing a number successively by 20 percent and 30 percent, it is decreased by 22 percent. Resultant value is what percentage of the required correct value?
questions.questionHtml: Instead of increasing a number successively by 20 percent and 30 percent, it is decreased by 22 percent. Resultant value is what percentage of the required correct value?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume the initial number is 100.

Required Correct Value = 100 × 1.20 × 1.30 = 156 units.

Actual Resultant Value = 100 − 22% of 100 = 78 units.

Required percentage = (Resultant ÷ Correct) × 100 = (78 ÷ 156) × 100 = 50%.

∴ The correct answer is 50 percent.

Alternate Method

Given:

Successive increases: 20% and 30%

Error decrease: 22%

Formula Used:

Net change for successive percentage a% and b% = [a + b + (a × b) / 100]%

Percentage relative value = (Value1 / Value2) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial number be x = 100.

⇒ Net successive increase = 20 + 30 + (20 × 30) / 100 = 50 + 6 = 56%.

⇒ Required correct value = 100 + 56% of 100 = 156.

⇒ Resultant value (after 22% decrease) = 100 − 22% of 100 = 78.

⇒ Percentage of correct value = (Resultant Value / Correct Value) × 100

⇒ Required percentage = (78 / 156) × 100

⇒ Required percentage = (1 / 2) × 100 = 50%.

∴ The correct answer is 50 percent.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of x% and y%, the effective change is given by the formula (x + y + xy/100)%. Use positive for increase and negative for decrease.

Multiplying Factor Method

An increase of r% is equivalent to multiplying the base by (1 + r/100), while a decrease of r% is equivalent to multiplying by (1 − r/100).

Percentage Comparison

To calculate what percent A is of B, use the formula (A ÷ B) × 100. Ensure both quantities are in the same units.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 30% voters did not cast their votes and 200 votes were declared invalid. The winner got 65% of the valid votes. If he won by 1200 votes, then find the total votes.
questions.questionHtml: In an election between two candidates, 30% voters did not cast their votes and 200 votes were declared invalid. The winner got 65% of the valid votes. If he won by 1200 votes, then find the total votes.
questions.solution:
Given:

30% voters did not cast their votes.

200 votes were declared invalid.

The winner got 65% of the valid votes.

The winner won by 1200 votes.

Formula Used:

Total votes = Valid votes + Invalid votes + Votes not cast

Calculation:

Let the total number of votes be V.

Votes cast = 70% of V = 0.7V

Valid votes = Votes cast - Invalid votes = 0.7V - 200

The winner got 65% of the valid votes.

Votes received by the winner = 0.65 × (0.7V - 200)

The loser got the remaining valid votes.

Votes received by the loser = (0.7V - 200) - 0.65 × (0.7V - 200)

The winner won by 1200 votes.

⇒ 0.65 × (0.7V - 200) - [(0.7V - 200) - 0.65 × (0.7V - 200)] = 1200

⇒ 0.65 × (0.7V - 200) - 0.35 × (0.7V - 200) = 1200

⇒ 0.3 × (0.7V - 200) = 1200

⇒ 0.21V - 60 = 1200

⇒ 0.21V = 1260

⇒ V = 1260 / 0.21

⇒ V = 6000

The total number of votes is 6000.

questions.question: In a two-candidate election, 10% of the voters did not cast their ballots. 10% of the votes cast were found invalid. The winning candidate received 54% of the valid votes and a 1620-vote majority. Find the number of people on the voter list who have registered to vote.
questions.questionHtml: In a two-candidate election, 10% of the voters did not cast their ballots. 10% of the votes cast were found invalid. The winning candidate received 54% of the valid votes and a 1620-vote majority. Find the number of people on the voter list who have registered to vote.
questions.solution:
Given:

10% of the voters did not cast their ballots

10% of the votes cast were found invalid

The winning candidate received 54% of the valid votes and a 1620-vote majority

Formula Used:

Value = Original Value x (100 - Percentage)/100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the total number of voter list registered be x 

10% of the voters did not cast their ballots means 90% of voters cast their ballots

⇒ Total voters cast their ballots = Original Value x (100 - Percentage)/100 = \(\frac{x\times 90}{100}\)

10% of the votes cast were found invalid means 90% of the votes were valid

⇒ Total valid votes = 90% of Total voters cast their ballots = \(\frac{x\times 90}{100}\times\frac{90}{100} = \frac{x\times 90\times 90}{10000}~\)

The winning candidate received 54% of the valid votes 

⇒ Winning candidates get votes = 54% of Total valid votes = \( \frac{x\times 90\times 90}{10000}\times \frac{54}{100}= \frac{x\times 90\times 90\times54}{1000000}~\)

The losing candidate gets 46% of the valid votes

⇒ Losing candidates get votes = 46% of Total the valid votes = \( \frac{x\times 90\times 90}{10000}\times \frac{46}{100}= \frac{x\times 90\times 90\times46}{1000000}~\)

as we know

The winning candidate won by a margin of 1620 votes

⇒ \(\frac{x\times 90\times 90\times54}{10000}- \frac{x\times 90\times 90\times46}{10000}=1620\)

⇒ \( \frac{x\times 90\times 90\times8}{10000}=1620~\)

⇒ x = 0.025 x 1000000 = 25000

Hence, The total number of voter lists registered is 25000.

questions.question: 150 litre mixture of milk and water contains 30 percent milk. How much more milk must be added to make water percentage in the mixture as 40 percent?
questions.questionHtml: 150 litre mixture of milk and water contains 30 percent milk. How much more milk must be added to make water percentage in the mixture as 40 percent?
questions.solution:
The volume of milk in the mixture is 30% of 150 litres = 0.3 × 150 = 45 litres. 

The volume of water in the mixture is 150 - 45 = 105 litres.

40% of water in mixture = 105 litres, 100% of mixture = 105/40 × 100 = 262.5

We need to add 262.5 - 150 = 112.5 liters

questions.question: P's income is 150 percent of Q's income and P's expenditure is 60 percent of Q's expenditure. If Q saves 20 percent of his income, then how much percentage does P save of his own income?
questions.questionHtml: P's income is 150 percent of Q's income and P's expenditure is 60 percent of Q's expenditure. If Q saves 20 percent of his income, then how much percentage does P save of his own income?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume Q's Income = 100 → Q's Savings = 20 → Q's Expenditure = 80.

P's Income = 150% of 100 = 150.

P's Expenditure = 60% of 80 = 48.

P's Savings = 150 − 48 = 102.

P's Saving Percentage = (102 ÷ 150) × 100 = 68%.

∴ The correct answer is 68%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Income of P = 150% of Income of Q

Expenditure of P = 60% of Expenditure of Q

Savings of Q = 20% of his Income

Calculations:

Let Income of Q = 100x

⇒ Savings of Q = 20% of 100x = 20x

⇒ Expenditure of Q = 100x − 20x = 80x

⇒ Income of P = 150% of 100x = 150x

⇒ Expenditure of P = 60% of 80x = 48x

⇒ Savings of P = Income of P − Expenditure of P

⇒ Savings of P = 150x − 48x = 102x

⇒ P's Savings Percentage = (102x ÷ 150x) × 100

⇒ P's Savings Percentage = (102 ÷ 1.5) = 68%

∴ The correct answer is 68%.

Additional Information

Basic Income Formula

Income = Expenditure + Savings. This is the fundamental equation for all budget-related problems.

Savings Percentage

Savings % = (Savings ÷ Income) × 100. This measures what portion of the total earnings is retained after expenses.

Ratio of Income & Expenditure

If the ratio of Income, Expenditure, and Savings is known for one person, it can be scaled using multipliers to compare with another person.

questions.question: Radha saves x% of her income. If her income increases by 28% and the expenditure increases by 20%, then her savings increase by 40%. What is the value of x ?
questions.questionHtml: Radha saves x% of her income. If her income increases by 28% and the expenditure increases by 20%, then her savings increase by 40%. What is the value of x ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the Alligation Method between Expenditure and Savings to find the ratio of Income components.

Expenditure increase (20%) and Savings increase (40%) result in a total Income increase (28%).

Ratio of Expenditure : Savings = (40 − 28) : (28 − 20) = 12 : 8 = 3 : 2.

Savings percentage (x) = [Savings / (Expenditure + Savings)] × 100 = [2 / (3 + 2)] × 100 = 40%.

∴ The correct answer is 40.

Alternate Method

Given: Savings = x% of Income, Income increase = 28%, Expenditure increase = 20%, Savings increase = 40%.

Formula Used: Income = Expenditure + Savings

⇒ Let Income be 100. Then Savings = x and Expenditure = 100 − x.

⇒ New Income = 100 × 1.28 = 128.

⇒ New Expenditure = (100 − x) × 1.20 = 120 − 1.2x.

⇒ New Savings = x × 1.40 = 1.4x.

⇒ New Income = New Expenditure + New Savings

⇒ 128 = (120 − 1.2x) + 1.4x

⇒ 128 − 120 = 0.2x

⇒ 8 = 0.2x

⇒ x = 8 / 0.2 = 40.

∴ The correct answer is 40.

Additional Information

Income-Expenditure Concept

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any percentage change in components must balance this equation.

Alligation in Income Problems

When two parts of a whole change by different percentages, the overall percentage change is the weighted average. The Alligation rule helps find the initial ratio of those parts.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective change is [a + b + (a×b)/100]%. This is useful for problems involving multiple increases/decreases.

questions.questionHtml: Sonam is a cab driver, who plies within a city. Given:

20% more than the number of kilometres

That she drives on Tuesday and she drives a total of 336 km on Wednesday.

questions.questionHtml: In an election between Sunita and Mamata, 85% of voters cast their votes but 2% of votes were invalid. If Sunita got 64,974, votes which is 78% of valid votes, then the total number of voters enrolled in the election was:
questions.solution:
0.85X = Total votes cast, 0.833X = Valid votes,

64,974 = 0.78 × 0.833X → 64,974 = 0.64974X → X = 64,974 / 0.64974 = 1,00,000
